findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime key used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw `cursor.value`. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `getattr` returns a `datetime` and `math.floor` raises `TypeError`. `DateTimePaginator` avoids this by converting through `strftime` with a multiplier and rebuilding a datetime from the cursor. Even if the key function worked, `build_queryset` would compare the `datetime` column to a raw millisecond integer. Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` that returns at least one row will therefore 500, or produce an invalid SQL comparison on the next page.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing is unsupported by Django and the comments claim otherwise
findings.body: The code does `queryset[cursor.offset : stop]` with a negative `cursor.offset`, and the comment says "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically". Django querysets raise on negative indexing ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so a client-supplied cursor such as `value:-5:0` produces a 500. The comments ("access data beyond normal pagination bounds", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") describe a capability that does not exist. They also invite a future change to bypass offset validation. Nothing validates or bounds the user-controlled offset.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator behavior changed for every consumer with a misleading rationale
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is used by many endpoints. A negative offset on a forward cursor used to fail; it is now silently clamped to 0, so a malformed cursor returns the first page instead of an error. For `is_prev`, negative offsets still reach `queryset[...]` and still crash. The later trim logic (`len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) still uses the unclamped `offset`, so it is inconsistent with the actual slice. The comment says the queryset "will handle boundary conditions", which is false. This change is unrelated to the spans buffer work in the PR title.

findings.title: Eager evaluation of `organization_context.member.has_global_access` can crash every request
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is computed on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set, as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be `None` (for example for org auth tokens or API keys with org:write that are not tied to a member). For such callers the existing audit-log endpoint now raises `AttributeError` and returns a 500, even though they never asked for the new feature. The check also uses `is_superuser` rather than `is_active_superuser`, so it ignores whether the superuser session is actually active. The new option should be evaluated lazily and `None`-safely, or not added at all.

findings.title: Redirect-chain depth limit silently cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The loop bound changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, and the comment documenting the limitation was deleted. This is unrelated to the eviction work and is not mentioned in the PR. Span trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now stop resolving early. The span is then attached to an intermediate set instead of the real segment, which fragments segments. The reduction should be justified or reverted.

findings.title: Eviction silently drops spans with a hard-coded limit and no signal
findings.body: When a segment has more than 1000 spans, `zpopmin` silently discards the earliest-ending ones. The old behavior logged an error and bumped the `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. The new path emits nothing, so truncated segments are invisible. The limit 1000 is hard-coded in Lua while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still a constructor argument that is no longer used anywhere, so configuration and behavior have diverged. Also, `zunionstore` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so a payload present in both sets (for example after a redelivery) gets its score added together. That distorts the eviction ordering, and `AGGREGATE MAX` or `MIN` would be correct.

findings.title: Switching key type from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight segments during deploy
findings.body: Segment keys (`span-buf:s:*`) change from sets (`sadd`/`sscan`/`scard`/`sunionstore`) to sorted sets (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zcard`/`zunionstore`) with no migration or versioned key prefix. Keys written by old consumers live up to `redis_ttl` (1h). Any new consumer touching an existing set-typed key, in `zadd`, in the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`, or in `zscan` on flush, gets a `WRONGTYPE` error. That fails the batch or the flusher and can crash-loop the consumer until the old keys expire or are flushed. A new key prefix, or a drain-before-deploy step, is needed.

findings.title: Comment claims Cursor allows negative offsets for 'efficient reverse pagination', but nothing changed
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination and enable efficient reverse pagination. `Cursor.__init__` still does `int(offset)` exactly as before, and downstream code cannot execute negative offsets (Django rejects negative slicing). The comment is misleading and documents a feature that is not implemented.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction behavior or the new paginator/endpoint path
findings.body: The tests only add the `end_timestamp_precise` argument to existing Span constructions. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans and checks that the lowest-score spans are evicted. There is none for eviction after a merge via `zunionstore` either, and none for the removal of the `max_segment_spans` check in `_load_segment_data`. There are also no tests for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, for the `optimized_pagination=true` branch of the audit-log endpoint, or for the paginator offset-clamping change. The new paginator and endpoint code would fail on first use (datetime key handling, negative slicing).
